html:
A dangerous escalation in the Middle East is dominating global affairs today, with Donald Trump threatening direct action against Iranian infrastructure and Iran confirming strikes on US military facilities and allied nations. Simultaneously, reports indicate the United States is poised to approve a significant nuclear deal allowing Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium, raising proliferation concerns.

US-Iran Conflict: Donald Trump has threatened to destroy Iranian bridges or power plants for each ship attack in the Strait of Hormuz, following the eleventh consecutive night of US strikes on Iran. In retaliation, Iran's Army and IRGC claim to have struck US military installations in Jordan and Bahrain, with Iran's Army also targeting a US command center in Kuwait. These strikes in Jordan resulted in two US service members killed and one missing, while Jordan reported intercepting multiple Iranian missiles and drones. Diplomatic efforts, reportedly involving Pakistan, Qatar, and Egypt, are underway to revive a ceasefire.

Regional Security & Energy: The Houthi movement has announced a "blockade for a blockade" in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, leading to Saudi oil tankers and other ships making sharp U-turns. This threatens to create a dual energy chokepoint crisis, jeopardizing approximately 6 million barrels of crude oil per day heading to Asia via the Red Sea and potentially the Suez Canal. The Strait of Hormuz is now a focal point of US-Iran escalation, with Iran warning it will not issue permits for passage as long as "aggression on Iran" continues. GCC and Arab states, including Saudi Arabia and Jordan, have condemned Houthi accusations and threats.

Ukraine & European Developments: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has replaced the country's army chief, Mykhailo Drapatyi, days after dismissing the defense minister, following a week of protests and reported feuding among military leaders. This leadership overhaul comes as Ukrainian drones struck Russian online giant retailer Wildberries' logistics hubs for a second time. Meanwhile, the European Union is attempting to finalize its 21st package of sanctions against Russia, even as the Venice Biennale challenges an EU decision to withdraw a grant over Russia's return to its 2026 edition. Separately, France recorded over 5,700 excess deaths during a recent June-July heatwave and approved a sweeping social media ban for children under 15.

Global Economy & Trade: Trade tensions have escalated between the US and Canada, leading to the cancellation of a joint celebration for the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge. This follows Donald Trump’s announcement of a 50% tariff on most Canadian goods, with his trade envoy facing Senate questioning regarding the "tariff spree" and its impact on American consumers. In technological news, top US AI developers Anthropic and OpenAI have voiced support for Australia's new AI regulations, signaling a broader global trend towards AI governance. India is also investing heavily to become a semiconductor hub, seeking to diversify global supply chains.

Other World Events: Daniel Siad, a modeling scout whose name appeared thousands of times in the Epstein files, was found dead near Paris. In Austria, a police station has opened at Adolf Hitler’s birthplace, a move aimed at deterring Nazi-linked pilgrimages. Liberia reported its largest-ever drug bust, seizing $370 million worth of cocaine. In Australia, a nationwide emergency warning system test, AusAlert, is scheduled for Monday, while emergency services are being trained in analog navigation techniques in preparation for potential satellite outages.
